study.title: Deep Learning-Based Approach to Automatically Assess Coronary Distensibility Following Kawasaki Disease

imaging.modality_detail: Invasive X-ray coronary angiography (pediatric X-ray angiograms) acquired during cardiac catheterization
imaging.territory_detail: Left and right coronary arteries in Kawasaki disease patients and controls

public_dataset_used.detail: Segmentation ground truth database of 100 pediatric X-ray angiograms; availability not stated

task.task_description: U-Net-like encoder-decoder segments the coronary artery tree on each angiographic frame across 1-2 cardiac cycles; centerlines and calibers are extracted to compute distensibility metrics (CSD, MCV, MEV) and elastic moduli, which are correlated with OCT damage scores and tracked longitudinally in Kawasaki disease patients.
task.clinical_application: Assessment of coronary artery distensibility/stiffness after Kawasaki disease (regressed vs persistent aneurysms)

temporal_evidence.quote: The coronary artery tree for each subject was automatically segmented (see Fig. 1) for each image/time point

G1.quote: due to the retrospective design of the study and small patient size

G5.quote: To reduce annotation time, we used segmentation maps from a neural network trained to segment retina vessels.

G6.quote: The prognostic value of microvascular changes on OCT and vascular stiffness could not be assessed due to the retrospective design of the study

G8.quote: Two elastic moduli were calculated for each subject from the above metrics of coronary artery distensibility and the subject's trans-myocardial blood pressure gradients

G11.quote: Future studies should evaluate the impact of distensibility on cardiac outcome following KD

other_limitations: OCT performed only in the left coronary artery while longitudinal analysis included both left and right branches
Evolution of distensibility in healthy controls could not be studied longitudinally
future_work: Evaluate the impact of distensibility on cardiac outcome following KD
Validate the method on coronary angiography obtained with cardiac CT
Apply automated distensibility analysis to prospectively stratified KD patients at risk of major adverse cardiac events
Extend to other types of vascular disease
